decision: How fast is our existing customer base leaking or growing, and which retention move should we fund first?
limitations: It reads one period at a time. A single month is not a trend; read the numbers against your own segment and your own history.

The projection repeats this period's rates every period. It is arithmetic, not a forecast: it ignores seasonality, cohort age and price changes, and with new business it assumes new customers retain like the base.

NRR and GRR are compared with reference points only for annual input, set for Series B/C enterprise software and bootstrapped $3M-$20M ARR SaaS. High NRR can hide heavy logo churn, so read GRR and logo churn alongside it.

An unrecognised field or a non-number stops the run and is named. It can't tell whether the amounts match the period you chose. One row per customer compares two dates, so a returning customer counts as new. The cap is 2,000 rows.
review: The finance lead confirms the period's movement reconciles to billing, that new business is kept out of expansion, and which period was used, before NRR or GRR goes to the board.
